# CameraView: a camera in your layout

<!-- Generated by dist/sdk/gen-widget-docs.py from the code. Do not edit by hand. -->

The camera component and its port.

## `cameraview`  (`crates/iyakki-ui-sdk/src/cameraview.rs`)

`CameraView`: live camera pictures as a component an SDK app places in its layout (docs/development/UI-SDK.md, "Embedding camera views").

The app keeps a `CameraView` in its state, gives it a [`CameraPort`] (the core's), a [`ViewConfig`] and an action number range, and a
rectangle to draw in. What the view shows, in the order a person meets it: the cameras the person may watch (a list to tick, or the
cameras the app named), the consent card ("Allow" and "Deny"; nothing is pulled before Allow), then the live pictures: one camera or a
grid of up to 4, a sign while pictures are being pulled, a name and a state sentence on each cell, the owner's motion zones and recent
motion boxes over the picture (read only), a REC mark on a camera that is being recorded, a snapshot button (a card every time), pan, tilt
and zoom buttons when the camera has them (a card the first time), full screen, and Close. A hidden view pulls nothing.

What the app does, in four lines:
```text
event(Tick(t)):  cams.tick(t)                         event(Action): if cams.owns(a) { cams.action(a) }
event(Key):      cams.key(k) while it has the focus   pane hidden or shown: cams.set_visible(v)
view:            cams.draw(c, th, &metrics, rect)     leaving the screen: cams.close()
```
Pictures are never queued: each tick the view asks for the newest one newer than what it has, at most 5 times a second for a grid cell and
10 for one large camera (the core's own caps), keeps one picture per camera, and draws it letterboxed with [`Canvas::image`]. Colours come
from the theme and sizes from the metrics only.

## `cameras`  (`crates/iyakki-ui-sdk/src/cameras.rs`)

The cameras port: what an SDK app is handed so that it can embed live camera pictures (see [`crate::cameraview::CameraView`]). Like the
storage and assistant ports it carries no device access: the host gives the app a port and the port is the core's. One port is one person
and one app (the host binds them), so no call names either; one port holds at most one view.

The host-side meaning, in one paragraph: the core lists the cameras this person may watch (and no others), opens a view only after the
person allowed its card, hands out only the newest picture of each camera, writes nothing for a view, saves a snapshot only into the
person's own folder after a card, moves a camera only after a card, and writes the audit line with names only. The port types below are
the SDK's own copies of the core's (`iyakki_core_api::cameras`), so this crate depends on no other IYAKKI crate; the host maps them.
[`MemCameras`] is the in-memory port for tests and the browser preview, with the same rules.

### trait `CameraPort`

The cameras of this host for one person and one app. A refusal is a sentence the view shows.

```rust
pub trait CameraPort
```

Methods:

- `fn list(&mut self) -> CamResult<Vec<CamInfo>>  // has a default`: The cameras the person may watch. Free: nothing starts.
- `fn open(&mut self, _cameras: &[String], _large: bool, _label: &str) -> CamResult<Vec<CamInfo>>  // has a default`: Make the view. Nothing is pulled until the person allows the card that [`CameraPort::events`] brings.
- `fn decide(&mut self, _call: &str, _approve: bool) -> CamResult<()>  // has a default`
- `fn state(&mut self) -> CamResult<ViewState>  // has a default`
- `fn set_visible(&mut self, _visible: bool) -> CamResult<()>  // has a default`
- `fn frame(&mut self, _camera: &str, _after: u64, _format: ImageFormat) -> CamResult<Option<Image>>  // has a default`: The newest picture of a camera newer than `after`, or `None`.
- `fn overlay(&mut self, _camera: &str) -> CamResult<Overlay>  // has a default`
- `fn snapshot(&mut self, _camera: &str) -> CamResult<String>  // has a default`: Ask to save one picture; the answer is the call id of the card.
- `fn ptz(&mut self, _camera: &str, _cmd: Ptz) -> CamResult<Option<String>>  // has a default`: A move: `Some(call)` when a card was shown for it, `None` when it ran.
- `fn events(&mut self) -> Vec<CamEvent>  // has a default`
- `fn close(&mut self)  // has a default`

### struct `MemCameras`

The in-memory port: scripted cameras and frames, the same rules as the core (consent first, hidden pulls nothing, a snapshot asks every
time, the first move asks), every effect recorded. Clone it: one clone goes to the view, the other stays with the test.

```rust
pub struct MemCameras
```

Methods:

- `pub fn new(app: &str) -> MemCameras`
- `pub fn add(&self, info: CamInfo)`
- `pub fn push_frame(&self, camera: &str, w: u32, h: u32, rgba: Vec<u8>) -> u64`: A new picture (RGBA); returns its sequence number.
- `pub fn push_solid(&self, camera: &str, w: u32, h: u32, rgb: [u8; 3]) -> u64`
- `pub fn set_status(&self, camera: &str, status: CamStatus, detail: &str)`
- `pub fn set_zones(&self, camera: &str, zones: Vec<Shape>)`
- `pub fn push_motion(&self, camera: &str, mark: Mark)`
- `pub fn no_screen(&self, on: bool)`: Every card is answered "no" by the system (no screen to ask on).
- `pub fn pulled(&self, camera: &str) -> u64`: Pictures handed out for a camera.
- `pub fn snapshots(&self) -> Vec<String>`
- `pub fn moves(&self, camera: &str) -> Vec<Ptz>`
- `pub fn audit(&self) -> Vec<String>`: Names only, like the core's lines.
- `pub fn calls(&self) -> Vec<String>`: The names of the port calls made, in order (`open`, `frame front`, `set_visible false`...), to prove what the view asked for.
